title: Determine the supported Beads read model
description:
## Question

Which supported Beads 1.x interfaces should a local read-only web application use to load current work items, labels, comments, statuses, parent links, blocking dependencies, and detect changes without corrupting or locking the repository? Compare CLI JSON, direct Dolt or SQL access, passive JSONL, and any supported API; identify compatibility and version constraints and recommend a boundary.
close_reason: Decision recorded: use version-gated, short-lived read-only bd CLI snapshots.

comments.author: Helio Pais
comments.text:
## Decision

Use the installed `bd` CLI as the sole Beads boundary. Read a complete local snapshot through a short-lived `bd --readonly -C <repository> export` process; normalize issues, labels, comments, raw statuses, parent-child links, and blocking dependency types in an app-owned adapter. Hydrate only missing dependency endpoints with bounded `bd --readonly ... show <id...> --json` calls so path-relevant system nodes can appear without loading all infrastructure or memories.

Require `bd >= 1.1.0, < 2.0.0`: 1.0.x has the JSON surface, but official 1.0.4 reports show nominal reads could mutate passive JSONL in embedded edge cases, while 1.1.0 explicitly guarantees read-only behavior through the embedded store. Detect change by polling short-lived exports and comparing a canonical content hash; retain the last good snapshot on transient lock/errors. Do not use long-lived `bd list --watch`, direct Dolt/SQL, passive `.beads/issues.jsonl`, implicit `bd dolt pull`, or MCP as the app data plane.

Primary sources:
- https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/v1.0.4/docs/COMMUNITY_TOOLS.md
- https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/v1.0.4/cmd/bd/export.go
- https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/v1.0.4/internal/types/types.go
- https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/v1.0.4/beads.go
- https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/releases/tag/v1.1.0
- https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/4033
- https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/3415
- https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md

Full rationale and local verification: `docs/research/beads-read-model.md` on branch `research/beads-read-model`, commit `fe6a01a` (https://github.com/heliopais/beads-map/commit/fe6a01a).

title: Define repository catalog failure and safety behavior
description:
## Question

How should the local repository catalog handle moved, deleted, duplicate, symlinked, non-Beads, unreadable, or concurrently modified repositories while protecting local path privacy and preserving the read-only boundary?
close_reason: Approved simplified repository identity, recovery, privacy, and read-only safety contract.

comments.author: Helio Pais
comments.text: Decision: Keep the repository-safety contract small and observable. A catalog entry represents one local working copy by canonical real path; path aliases deduplicate, distinct copies remain separate, and Beads project identity validates only user-directed relocation. Missing, unreadable, or invalid entries remain visible with Retry, Locate, and catalog-only Remove; a running app may retain its last good graph only as visibly stale in memory, never across restart. Validate selected paths read-only against the supported Beads version and expected project without initializing, migrating, repairing, syncing, or running corrective commands. Keep catalog paths and view metadata in protected local app data, persist no issue content, minimize full-path display, and perform no scanning or network disclosure. Never interfere with concurrent Beads activity; replace the graph only from a complete snapshot for the expected repository. Retry, timeout, and process-scheduling mechanics belong to the architecture decision.

title: Define progress and roll-up semantics
description:
## Question

Which counts, percentages, and roll-ups should the execution summary and epic nodes present, and how should they treat missing estimates, compact system nodes, deferred work, closed work, and parent-child organization without misleading the user?
close_reason: Minimal count-based progress and direct-child epic roll-up semantics approved and recorded.

comments.author: Helio Pais
comments.text: Paused without resolution at user direction: the immediate goal is a simple working dependency-graph POC, not progress or roll-up specification.

comments.author: Helio Pais
comments.text: Resumed at user direction with a deliberately minimal target: retain execution-state counts, use simple issue-count roll-ups, and exclude estimate-weighted or nested percentage machinery unless a concrete need emerges.

comments.author: Helio Pais
comments.text: Decision: Keep the repository execution summary as unweighted counts across the five derived execution states; do not calculate an overall completion percentage. An epic may show only a simple completed / total roll-up over its direct human-facing child work items. A child counts as completed only when closed in Beads; deferred children remain in the denominator and incomplete, while system records are excluded. Do not recurse into descendants, weight estimates, or infer progress from missing estimates. The roll-up is informational and never replaces the epic's raw Beads status; an epic with no direct children shows no fraction.

title: Choose the graph workspace interaction model
description:
## Question

Which concrete graph-first layout and interaction model best communicates dependency direction, execution state, completed work, epic styling, selected details, and repository switching while remaining keyboard- and color-accessible?
close_reason: Approved graph workspace interaction model recorded with linked prototype.

comments.author: Helio Pais
comments.text:
## Decision

Adopt the approved graph-first workspace interaction model:

- App chrome contains the active repository switcher. A compact execution summary and separate epic context sit above the dependency graph; selecting a work item reveals details beside the graph on wide screens and below it on narrow screens.
- Lay out the DAG in stable left-to-right layers, from blockers to dependent outcomes. Preserve existing positions across refresh, support pan and zoom, and offer explicit re-layout. Do not support persisted manual node arrangement in the first release.
- Encode execution state redundantly with border accent, icon, and text. Keep work-item type separate, give epics the stronger type accent, keep completed work readable at reduced contrast, and emphasize selection plus its dependency path.
- Click or Enter selects a node without navigating away. Relationship-aware arrow keys move among blockers, dependents, and peers; Escape clears selection; assistive output announces type, execution state, and relationship.
- Remember viewport, selection, and completed-work visibility per repository. Switching repositories loads the latest local snapshot into the same shell and restores that repository view; a failed switch leaves the current graph intact.

Approved prototype: https://github.com/heliopais/beads-map/blob/main/docs/prototypes/graph-workspace.html

title: Define graph navigation, filtering, and scale guarantees
description:
## Question

What default filters, search behavior, path-focus controls, layout-stability guarantees, and repository-size targets must the first release support, and when should it cluster, virtualize, or ask the user to narrow the graph?
close_reason: Approved graph navigation, filtering, layout-stability, and scale contract recorded.

comments.author: Helio Pais
comments.text: Decision: Default to the complete human-facing repository graph, including unlinked work. Search locates without filtering; explicit state/type/label/assignee filters preserve real paths with compact context nodes; selection offers transitive Blockers, Dependents, and Both focus. Exploration preserves positions and dependency changes relayout only affected components. Support up to 1,000 displayed nodes and 3,000 edges, with 2-second usability at 500/1,500 and 5 seconds at the maximum; above that, show complete counts and an explicit narrowing gate. Do not semantically cluster; virtualization must preserve all full-graph behavior.

title: Specify the Beads Map read-only dependency explorer
description:
## Destination

Produce a build-ready product and technical specification for Beads Map: a CLI-launched, local, read-only web application that lets a developer inspect current work and its dependency graph for one Beads repository at a time, while switching among repositories without aggregating their graphs.

## Notes

Use the `grilling` and `domain-modeling` skills for human decision tickets. This map plans the product and technical specification; implementation is outside the map.

Standing boundaries fixed while charting:
- The graph workspace is the primary surface.
- Dependency edges represent blocking only; parent-child organization is separate.
- Human-facing work records are normal nodes; path-relevant system records may appear compactly.
- Closed work remains connected and dimmed by default.
- Execution state is derived as Completed, In progress, Ready, Blocked, or Deferred.
- The active graph auto-refreshes while preserving view state.
- The repository catalog is explicit, local, recent/pinned, and never aggregates graphs.
- Current state only; no historical time travel.

Primary upstream reference: https://github.com/gastownhall/beads

## Decisions so far

<!-- Closed decision tickets are indexed here. -->

- [Determine the supported Beads read model](beads:beads-map-lnd.7): Use short-lived, read-only `bd export` snapshots with targeted `show` hydration behind a tolerant adapter; require Beads >=1.1,<2 and poll/hash snapshots instead of reading Dolt/JSONL or using `--watch`.

- [Choose the graph workspace interaction model](beads:beads-map-lnd.1): Use a graph-first shell with a stable left-to-right DAG, accessible redundant state and type cues, in-context details, relationship-aware keyboard navigation, and per-repository view restoration.

- [Define graph navigation, filtering, and scale guarantees](beads:beads-map-lnd.2): Show the whole repository by default; separate locating, filtering, and path focus; preserve layout; support 1,000 nodes/3,000 edges with an explicit scale gate above it; virtualize without semantic clustering or data omission.

- [Define repository catalog failure and safety behavior](beads:beads-map-lnd.4): Identify and recover local working copies without merging them, keep catalog paths private, never mutate or interfere with Beads, and retain failed reads only as visibly stale in-memory graphs.

- [Define progress and roll-up semantics](beads:beads-map-lnd.6): Keep the summary as execution-state counts; epic roll-ups are unweighted completed / total counts over direct human-facing children, include deferred work as incomplete, exclude system records, and never override raw epic status.

- [Define the CLI lifecycle and distribution contract](beads:beads-map-lnd.3): Expose a foreground `beads-map` command installed with `uv tool`; auto-open a loopback browser session, choose a free default port, preserve catalog-first repository selection, support macOS first, update only on explicit user command, and stop with `Ctrl-C`.

## Not yet specified

- Exact implementation stack, process boundaries, testing strategy, and compatibility policy beyond what becomes clear from the read-model research and interaction prototype.
- The final specification packaging and handoff shape after product and architecture decisions converge.

## Out of scope

- Creating, editing, claiming, closing, or otherwise mutating Beads records.
- Cross-repository dependency graphs or aggregate portfolio views.
- Hosted service, team collaboration, or stakeholder-reporting features.
- Historical playback, trends, or state-as-of views.
- Implementing the application within this Wayfinder effort.

title: Define the CLI lifecycle and distribution contract
description:
## Question

What invocation, repository selection, browser-launch, local-server lifecycle, port-conflict, supported-platform, installation, upgrade, and shutdown behavior belongs in the first release?
close_reason: CLI lifecycle and uv-tool distribution contract approved and recorded.

comments.author: Helio Pais
comments.text: Resumed at user direction with the working POC as the baseline: preserve its dependency-free local server, repository catalog, and browser UI unless a lifecycle requirement proves a concrete change is needed.

comments.author: Helio Pais
comments.text: Accepted distribution direction: the first release is installed user-wide as an isolated uv tool and exposes the  command. Use , , and ; allow an initial Git-source install before package-index publication. The existing  invocation remains the source-checkout fallback.

comments.author: Helio Pais
comments.text: Correction: the immediately preceding comment lost its inline command names because the shell interpreted backticks. The accepted distribution direction is: install the first release user-wide as an isolated uv tool exposing the `beads-map` command; use `uv tool install beads-map`, `uv tool upgrade beads-map`, and `uv tool uninstall beads-map`; allow a Git-source install before package-index publication; retain `python3 beads_map.py` as the source-checkout fallback. This comment supersedes the malformed one.

comments.author: Helio Pais
comments.text: Decision: Preserve the working POC lifecycle behind a packaged public command. The first release exposes `beads-map [repository ...]`; `python3 beads_map.py` remains the source fallback. Install, upgrade, and uninstall through `uv tool`, initially allowing Git-source installation; perform no automatic update checks or self-modification. Official support is macOS, with Linux best-effort through CLI-supplied paths and Windows out of scope. Run one loopback-only foreground server, open the default browser unless `--no-browser` is set, keep running when tabs close, and stop with `Ctrl-C`; provide no daemon, tray, or login-start behavior. Try port 8765 by default and automatically choose another loopback port if it is occupied, but treat an explicit `--port` as strict. With supplied repositories, remember all and select the first. With no arguments, restore the last catalog selection; on an empty catalog use the current directory if it is a valid Beads repository, otherwise open the empty app so the user can choose a folder.
